name: Viscera Gyre
description: Viscera Gyre is a turbulent gas giant whose atmosphere appears to churn like exposed internal organs, swirling masses of red, purple, and sickly yellow gases rolling over each other in constant upheaval. The planet sits at the edge of a dense asteroid belt, and its gravity constantly pulls debris into its atmosphere, where incoming rocks burn in long, bright streaks across the cloud tops. A thin ring of captured material orbits at a precarious angle, slowly being absorbed.

The toxic atmosphere emits radio noise across a broad spectrum, a crackling static that increases in intensity near the storm centers and creates interference zones that extend well beyond the planet's orbital space. The visual effect of the churning atmosphere is deeply unsettling, the colors and movements evoking organic processes more than meteorological ones. Pilots who spend too long in visual range report unease and a compulsive desire to look away.

A navigation beacon was placed in stable orbit generations ago to help ships traverse the adjacent asteroid belt, but the planet's expanding debris ring has complicated the approach path repeatedly, requiring periodic beacon relocation. A graveyard of satellites and probes that failed to adjust for the ring's growth tumbles through the outer orbital zone, their signals creating ghost readings that confuse automated navigation systems.

The helium-3 reserves in Viscera Gyre's atmosphere are substantial, but the constant asteroid bombardment and toxic radio interference make harvesting operations significantly more dangerous than at comparable gas giants. The navigation beacon is critical infrastructure for the asteroid belt trade routes, and its maintenance contract is one of the most hazardous and best-compensated in the sector. Plans to establish a permanent station have been repeatedly proposed and abandoned as the orbital environment continues to deteriorate.
